section.title: Every Body We Buried to Get Here
section.form_description: A speech meant to move someone to act — the narrator talking Shepard (or whoever is listening) up off the floor and back into the fight. Sections are the rising beats of an address: the stakes named, the doubt named plainly, the evidence from a life lived that it can be done, the call. The narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it — but so is the listener's: the narrator holds up the other person's record as often as their own, since it's their record the speech is meant to land on.
section.form_note:
The brief is a speech, not a life story: Jack talking Shepard up in the last hour before the last push, using her own record as proof it can be done. Set after the Cerberus coup, the Citadel DLC shore leave, and the Cronos Station assault, this is the morning of the London conduit assault on Earth — everything is already staged (ships loaded, the plan set, the crew briefed), and the only thing left to do is get up and launch it. Jack is rousing Shepard right before he walks out to fight, not settling him in for the night. Romanced Jack per canon.choices (romance: Jack), consummated per jack_meeting/normandy-engineering scene at the end of ME2, with the Citadel DLC back tattoo. Note: choices.yaml's citadel_coup detail says Thane "died protecting the dalatrass," but the event record (thane-krios-death-defending-the-salarian-councilor) and the coup scene (citadel-coup-csec-office-kai-leng) both have him dying for the Salarian Councilor — treating this as the user's shorthand slip, not a real contradiction, and writing it as the Councilor. Per Thomas's request, "what-cerberus-made-me-for" and "the-kids-at-grissom" were rebuilt off shared Shepard/Jack history and broader lore instead of the Teltin and Grissom backstory events: recruitment off the Purgatory prison ship (jack-recruitment-purgatory) plus the Jack/Miranda confrontation Shepard settled (jack_miranda_dispute: appeased both), and the Suicide Mission itself (Jack held the biotic barrier, all-survived outcome per suicide_mission canon). Pragia/Teltin and Grissom get at most a glancing bridging mention, never the anchor. Jack's framing of "holding a barrier is a focus problem, not a strength problem" and "Cerberus bought a weapon and Shepard made a person" are her own editorializing on the record, not new corpus facts.
Revision per Thomas: Shepard's own AU record is now a load-bearing second thread, not a token mention. Jack is pitching HIM back to himself — every section now carries at least one beat where she cites something true of Shepard specifically as the proof, not just her own Purgatory/barrier/Brimstone/Murtock record. Sourced from config/canon/choices.yaml's Shepard AU overrides (Normandy-born, no parents, gang and drug problem before Anderson pulled him into N7; Sole Survivor of Akuze, the whole squad dead but him; Vanguard, biotic charge into the guns; alignment "Paragon, except against oppressors"; first name Thomas) plus the ME2/ME3 record most relevant to a focus-and-resolve pitch: Cerberus rebuilding him from a corpse via the Lazarus Project (a direct mirror to Jack's own tank), Mordin's death at the Shroud finishing the genophage cure, and Thessia — the one fight where Kai Leng actually got the better of him and walked off with Vendetta, which Jack uses as the counter-example, not the insult. Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station, days earlier in the same push on Cerberus's headquarters, closes the speech as proof the focus she's asking for is already proven, not a new trick.
Second revision per Thomas, correcting two errors: (1) the outline had previously let the closing section cite the Illusive Man's suicide as settled proof Jack could point back to. That confrontation happens on the Citadel, concurrent with or immediately after the London conduit assault itself — part of the endgame this speech is walking Shepard out the door toward, not something resolved before it. It has been cut entirely; Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station (a distinct, already-resolved event from the assault on Cerberus's headquarters, which happened before this morning) carries that closing beat on its own. (2) the whole episode was misdated as the evening before, ending in the two of them going to sleep. It is corrected throughout to the morning of the assault itself: the fleet is already massed, the plan already briefed, nothing left to prepare — Jack is waking Shepard and getting him moving, not tucking him in. No section still ends on rest; every "tonight"/"tomorrow" reference has been changed to "today," "now," or "in the next hour," and "The Last Quiet Night" is renamed "The Last Quiet Hour" to hold the tattoo-and-sentiment beat inside a tense pre-launch hush instead of an evening of repose. The Crucible's final choice and Shepard's fate at the end of it remain deliberately left out: that hasn't happened yet either, and reaching for it would still be narrator omniscience, not something Jack could actually voice this morning.
This does not strain the form. `motivational`'s brief is explicit that "the narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it" — and Jack's whole method here is to make Shepard's history do exactly that work on Shepard himself: he's not telling her own story for its own sake, she's holding up his record as the evidence because a room full of only Jack's proof lets him nod along without it landing on him. Spine stays `mixed` — some sections anchor to Jack's own events/scenes, some to Shepard's, most to both at once, which is precisely what a speech that argues from the listener's own life looks like structurally. No change to form.

required_facts.fact: Following the destruction of Arcturus Station and the Alliance Parliament, Councilor Donnel Udina became the most powerful remaining political figure in the Systems Alliance government. Desperate to retake Earth and frustrated by the Council's refusal to grant him emergency powers and direct Citadel forces to the Alliance's aid, Udina negotiated a deal with Cerberus. The plan was to stage a bloodless coup: arrest the Council and force them to grant Udina emergency authority to command the Citadel Fleet to Earth. When the Salarian Councilor discovered Udina's betrayal, the coup rapidly deteriorated into a massacre. Cerberus operatives, led by assassin Kai Leng, stormed the Citadel, issuing martial law and murdering both C-Sec officers and civilians. Kai Leng pursued the Council members as they attempted to escape. However, Commander Shepard intercepted Leng at the elevator leading to the Council's escape shuttle, which Cerberus had already destroyed, trapping the Councilors inside. When Shepard entered the elevator shaft, they confronted Udina, the three Councilors, and the Virmire survivor (either Gunnery Chief Ashley Williams or Staff Lieutenant Kaidan Alenko), who was serving as the Council's bodyguard. Udina attempted to frame Shepard as Cerberus's accomplice, using fabricated video evidence and editing of the Salarian Councilor's death. In response, Udina tried to override the elevator doors to let in Cerberus operatives. The Asari Councilor physically interfered, and Udina violently shoved her aside while brandishing a pistol—creating the critical moment of decision. The Virmire survivor's trust in Shepard—built or eroded over their interactions across all three games—determined the outcome. Per `citadel_coup`, multiple factors influenced whether the survivor sided with Shepard or Udina: whether Shepard had romanced them in ME1, whether Shepard had cheated on them in ME2, whether Shepard had saved the Council, whether close companions survived to present, whether Shepard was kind during Priority: Mars, hospital visits, and admission of past wrongs. A trust threshold of 4+ resulted in automatic loyalty; below 0 meant they would turn against Shepard; between 0-3 required a Paragon interrupt to convince them to stand down. In the aftermath, while Shepard was granted mandatory shore leave by Joker, a Cerberus clone of the Commander—created in the weeks before the coup—executed a separate operation to seize control of the Normandy SR-2. The clone, operating through intermediaries and mercenary group CAT6, attempted to obtain Shepard's Spectre codes and command authority. During a confrontation at a sushi restaurant on the Silversun Strip, the clone's operative Brooks and a team of CAT6 mercenaries engaged Shepard and allies, but the original Commander escaped. The clone then used the stolen Spectre codes to breach the Citadel Archives, setting a trap that resulted in Shepard's squad being locked in an iridium vault. Escaping the vault, Shepard pursued the clone to the Citadel Docks. At the docking bay, Shepard boarded the Normandy as it was launching, fighting through waves of CAT6 mercenaries (Heavies, Snipers, Specialists) and Disruption Drones. Communications Specialist Samantha Traynor, who had been relieved of duty by the clone under false pretenses, assisted Shepard in breaching the sealed airlock using her mass-effect toothbrush. Inside the ship, Shepard's squad fought through the CIC toward the Cargo Bay, where the clone—now wearing full N7 armor—made its stand. As the Normandy attempted to launch from the Citadel, the showdown escalated into a two-stage fight between the original and clone Shepard, with Brooks providing sniper support. Shepard's loyal squadmates and pilot Cortez, working with Joker, managed to prevent the ship's FTL jump, leaving the shuttle bay doors open. During the final melee, both Shepards tumbled toward the open bay doors. Shepard's crew—"the emotional baggage" the clone had dismissed—pulled the original Commander to safety, while the clone, refusing aid and realizing it lacked what made Shepard truly human, fell to its death. Brooks was either arrested or killed depending on Shepard's final choice. With the threat neutralized, control of the Normandy was restored to Shepard, and Joker began planning a celebration with Traynor, EDI, Cortez, and other crew members.

During Cerberus's 2186 coup attempt on the Citadel (Priority: The Citadel II), Councilor Udina moved the Citadel Council toward a waiting escape shuttle while the Cerberus assassin Kai Leng hunted them. The salarian councilor - Valern, or Esheel if Valern had died on Sur'Kesh - hid under tactical cloak in the executor's cafe/office area after the executor was killed. When Commander Shepard's squad located him, he began to reveal that Udina was orchestrating the coup, and Kai Leng arrived to silence him. What happened next depended on who was still alive to intervene (per `citadel_coup` and `salarian_councilor`). If Thane Krios had survived the 2185 Suicide Mission and Shepard had visited him at Huerta Memorial Hospital before this mission, Thane dropped in and fought Kai Leng hand to hand, buying time and saving the councilor but taking Leng's blade through the torso. If Thane was absent but Major Kirrahe had survived Virmire in 2183 (per `kirrahe_virmire`), a cloaked Kirrahe took the shot meant for the councilor, then limped a short distance before collapsing and dying on the spot; as he was never Normandy crew, his name does not appear on the memorial wall. If neither was present - or no Mass Effect 2 save was imported - Kai Leng killed the salarian councilor outright. In every case Leng then fled, disabled Shepard's pursuit skycar with his sword, and ultimately escaped the failed coup. A mortally wounded Thane was taken to Huerta Memorial. Shepard could be present for his final moments, where his estranged son Kolyat joined them regardless of the outcome of Thane: Sins of the Father. In the last stage of Kepral's Syndrome, Thane died in surgery as Kolyat and Shepard recited the drell prayer to Kalahira; Thane revealed the prayer had been his wish for Shepard, not himself. His name was added to the Normandy's memorial wall. If Thane had survived Mass Effect 2 but was never visited at the hospital, he did not appear at the coup at all, yet his name still turned up on the memorial wall afterward. Shepard later avenged him by killing Kai Leng at Cerberus Headquarters.

To seal the turian-krogan alliance, the Urdnot leader (Wrex or Wreav) demands the genophage be cured. Once Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks has stabilised Eve and prepared the cure, Shepard leads a joint turian-krogan strike on Tuchanka to disperse it through the Shroud, the atmospheric tower above the krogan homeworld. Before the operation, Dalatrass Linron privately offers Shepard a deal: the salarians will back the war effort if Shepard lets Mordin secretly sabotage the cure, keeping the krogan weakened. Shepard can accept, refuse, or tell the krogan leader. The krogan convoy drives for the Shroud but is halted when Kalros, the largest known thresher maw, is roused in the catacombs beneath an abandoned krogan city and destroys a bridge. A Reaper Destroyer guards the Shroud. Eve proposes activating the ancient Maw Hammers to summon Kalros against the Reaper while the cure is completed. Shepard activates the hammers; Kalros drags the Destroyer down. The Shroud is left damaged and unstable, and the cure must be released manually from the top of the collapsing tower. The outcome is choice-conditional. If Shepard preserved Maelon's data in Mass Effect 2 (per `mordin_loyalty`) and did not accept the sabotage, Eve survives the procedure and the krogan gain a healthy future. If Maelon's data was destroyed, Eve dies of complications regardless. If Mordin is alive and the cure is genuine, he insists on going up the tower himself and is killed when it detonates, singing as he dies; if the cure is sabotaged and Mordin realises, Shepard can shoot him, or he goes up to fix it and dies anyway. If Padok Wiks replaced Mordin, Wiks dies in the tower. A sabotaged cure can also be carried out with the krogan none the wiser, especially under Wreav (per `genophage`: cured, or secretly sabotaged). Whatever happens, the Reaper guarding the Shroud is destroyed and the krogan commit forces to the war; a genuine cure earns their full strength, while sabotage risks later exposure.

evidence.text: “They're a bunch of self\-concerned jackasses, Shepard. We may have a spot on the Council, but humanity will always be considered second\-rate.” By 2186, Udina replaces Anderson as Councilor, if Anderson was originally nominated to the post by Shepard. After the destruction of Arcturus Station and death of the Alliance Parliament and Prime Minister Amul Shastri, Udina is left the most powerful political figure in the Alliance government. He is furious at the Council's refusal to work together but vows to do his best. Agreeing with Shepard and Admiral Hackett’s plan to construct the Crucible, Udina uses all political channels to aid in the war effort. He institutes a draft in all Alliance colonies, pressures colony worlds and allies for resources and ensures Hackett is provided with the resources and manpower to restore the remaining Fleets. Udina also provides Shepard with a perspective on the other Councilors to help the Commander find a way to pressure them for aid. During this time, Udina appoints the Virmire survivor, Kaidan Alenko/Ashley Williams, as the second human Spectre. He also submits a Council motion that converts a portion of Presidium docks into civilian emergency housing to accommodate the influx of refugees. Despite all these, Udina is left helpless when the Council refuses to give the Alliance support in retaking Earth. Horrified and panicked, Udina grows increasingly frustrated and desperate to help his homeworld. He confesses to Shepard that he knew a lot of people on Arcturus Station on a first name basis, requiring a second VI to keep track of their birthdays and anniversaries. Eventually, Udina's desperation leads him to a deal with Cerberus to instigate a bloodless coup of the Citadel, arrest the Council and force them to grant him the emergency power necessary to order all Citadel forces to Earth. The Salarian Councilor instantly detects Udina's suspicious actions and acquires evidence of his dealings. The resulting rush to conquer the Citadel and silence the Councilor, as well as the vastly differing goals of Udina and Kai Leng, who is responsible for leading Cerberus forces during the coup attempt, leads to the coup degenerating into a massacre, with Cerberus issuing martial law on the Citadel and murdering both C\-Sec officers and civilians alike. Meanwhile, Udina leads the remaining Councilors to an escape vehicle that Cerberus had already destroyed, allowing Kai Leng to corner them. This plan is undone when Shepard beats Leng to the Council and seals the entrance, blocking Leng’s path. Shepard confronts Udina, the Councilors, and Ashley Williams/Kaidan Alenko (who is acting as the Council's bodyguard) about Udina's treachery. In response, Udina tries to frame Shepard as being in league with Cerberus, even using edited footage of the Salarian Councilor's death as "evidence" of this treachery if the latter was killed. In the resulting conflict, Udina attempts to override the door's lock and open entry for the Cerberus operatives pursuing the Council. The Asari Councilor interferes, and in response Udina shoves her aside and threatens her with a pistol, resulting in him being shot and killed by either Shepard or the Virmire survivor. Meanwhile Leng, realizing his mission has failed as C\-Sec is close on his heels, abandons Udina to his fate. Later, when Shepard and Anderson are pondering Udina's reasons for the coup, they discuss whether he may have been indoctrinated, but ultimately they can only speculate.

evidence.text: By 2186 CE, the Council is forced to acknowledge the existence of the Reapers when the race of machines launch a full\-scale assault against the galaxy. Donnel Udina serves as humanity's representative to the Council regardless of previous circumstances, Anderson having resigned and resumed Alliance duties if he originally had the post. Though Shepard and Councilor Udina attempt to petition the Council for aid in retaking Earth, the Council races are more concerned with protecting their own borders. Thus, the Commander is forced to help the Council deal with their own problems in order to gain their support. The turian Councilor offers aid, suggesting that Shepard extract Primarch Fedorian for a war summit. The asari Councilor declines to participate in the summit, believing that the disputes between the krogan, turians, and salarians were too contentious to overcome and any summit would not succeed. After Shepard secures a krogan\-turian alliance by dealing with the genophage, the salarian Councilor requests via vidcomm that the Commander come to the Citadel. The Councilor reveals that Udina had been using his authority to move vast sums of money for unspecified purposes and wants to investigate these illicit activities. But just when Shepard returns to the Citadel, the Council suffers a betrayal from within. In desperation, Udina reached out to Cerberus and assisted them in launching a coup. Dealing with Cerberus forces along the way, Shepard meets the salarian Councilor, who had separated from the others. This Councilor warns the Commander of Udina's treachery, having learned of it beforehand and that Udina was leading the rest of the Council into a trap laid by Cerberus assassins. Meanwhile, one of Cerberus' top agents, Kai Leng, decloaks and attempts to assassinate the Councilor while the opportunity presents itself. Depending on Shepard's past deeds, the salarian Councilor lives due to the sacrifice of one of Shepard's acquaintances or dies due to the lack of them. In due course, Shepard is then able to find the other Councilors and reveals Udina's treachery, though Udina tries to paint the Commander as a Cerberus agent. If Shepard saved the old Council they recall the last time they didn't trust Shepard, however, and if not, the new Councilors reserve a bit more judgment on Shepard's claims. Whichever the case, Udina tries to escape and draws a gun on the asari Councilor, forcing Shepard or Kaidan/Ashley to shoot and kill him. The Councilors express gratitude to Shepard for saving them and offer their assistance in construction of the Crucible. The asari Councilor later contacts Shepard after the quarian\-geth conflict's resolution. Meeting in Udina's office, this councilor reveals there is an artifact on Thessia that could reveal the nature of the final piece of the Crucible: the Catalyst. The artifact is later revealed to be a Prothean beacon, only known to the highest levels of the asari government, due to Council laws forbidding the withholding of Prothean technology. Shepard fails to obtain the information within, causing the asari Councilor to break contact during the post\-mission report, claiming to make contingencies for the continuity of civilization.
evidence.for_key: the Cerberus coup on the Citadel and Udina's betrayal

evidence.text: Councilor Udina's attempted coup will no doubt be analyzed for generations to come, but a clear picture is beginning to emerge. Udina had contacted Cerberus to coordinate what was intended to be a bloodless takeover of the Citadel, in which he would force the other councilors to grant him emergency powers so that he could command the Citadel Fleet. He would then direct the fleet to liberate his homeworld, Earth. The plan fell apart early when Executor Pallin and the salarian councilor caught wind of it. In defense of the plan, the Illusive Man dispatched his top assassins, commanded by Kai Leng, to kill them. Udina had little choice but to support the assassins with an armed force sufficient to hold the Citadel. Captured confidantes have indicated that Udina and Leng's alliance was relatively fragile: Udina may have planned to turn on Cerberus once the fleet was his to command, and Leng departed when he calculated that Udina would not succeed. Persistent rumors suggest that Udina might have been a high\-functioning victim of Reaper indoctrination. His actions played right into the Reapers' plans: even if the coup failed, it would damage Citadel governance. If it succeeded, his plan to retake Earth would likely have turned into a military blunder that Council forces could ill afford. However, there is no direct evidence of his indoctrination, nor obvious opportunity. It is more likely that Udina acted out of desperation, and in doing so, cost humanity its councilor.
evidence.for_key: the Cerberus coup on the Citadel and Udina's betrayal

evidence.text:
This page is a chronological plot synopsis of the Mass Effect 3-era fiction.

In Mass Effect: Retribution, the Illusive Man had Kai Leng abduct former operative Paul Grayson and infected him with Reaper nanotech; Grayson, turned into a Reaper puppet, was hunted across the galaxy and finally killed at Grissom Academy by David Anderson, Kahlee Sanders and the student Nick. Mass Effect: Inquisition followed C-Sec's Bailey investigating Executor Pallin's supposed corruption at Udina's direction. Mass Effect: Deception continued the Kai Leng, Gillian Grayson and Biotic Underground threads. Mass Effect: Conviction had James Vega brought aboard the Normandy SR-2 to guard the imprisoned Shepard after the Bahak incident. Mass Effect: Invasion recounted Cerberus general Oleg Petrovsky and Colonel Raymond Ashe using an engineered Adjutant crisis to seize Omega from Aria T'Loak, who surrendered the station rather than see it destroyed. Mass Effect: Infiltrator followed rogue Cerberus operative Randall Ezno turning against the Director's Reaper-tech experiments after they mutilated his handler Inali Renata. Homeworlds #4 followed Liara T'Soni, now the Shadow Broker, chasing Prothean leads to Thessia and Kahje.

The Mass Effect 3 recap covered the Reaper invasion of Earth and Anderson staying behind; the Mars Archives and the discovery of the Prothean device (Crucible), with the android Eva Coré and EDI; the war summit and the genophage cure arc on Sur'Kesh and Tuchanka (Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks, Urdnot Wrex or Wreav, Dalatrass Linron, Primarch Adrien Victus, and Eve); the Cerberus coup on the Citadel and Udina's exposure and death; the quarian-geth war over Rannoch, ending in the destruction of a Reaper and peace or genocide; the fall of Thessia and Kai Leng's theft of the Prothean VI data; the pursuit of Cerberus through Sanctuary (Henry, Miranda and Oriana Lawson) to Cronos Station and Leng's death; and the battle for Earth. The synopsis closed with the Illusive Man's death, Anderson's death, and the Catalyst offering Shepard the Destroy, Control, Synthesis or refusal endings, followed by extensive epilogue variations and the Stargazer framing scene.
evidence.for_key: the Cerberus coup on the Citadel and Udina's betrayal

evidence.text: This was a short fetch mission in Mass Effect 3, available after Priority: The Citadel II. An asari scientist seated near the Bank area of the Presidium Commons, found only after Shepard stops Udina's coup, needed a statue from the asari Hesperia period for classified Crucible research because it bore highly accurate Prothean inscriptions and she had no images of it. Shepard obtained the statue by scanning the gas giant Polissa in the Vernio system of the Athena Nebula; it could alternatively be recovered through a Search and Rescue operation, in which case the journal entry was labeled Citadel: Hesperia Period Statue. Delivering it to the asari granted 5 Reputation, 15,000 credits, and an upgrade to the Alliance Engineering Corps War Asset.

evidence.text: This is a simple conversation\-only mission. To begin the mission, travel back to the Citadel. Once you have arrived, travel to the Citadel Embassies and make your way to the late Councilor Udina's office. Enter to trigger a cutscene. The asari Councilor will tell you that the Asari Republic has taken a turn for the worse, and will proceed to tell you that a Prothean artifact is hidden in the Temple of Athame on the asari homeworld, Thessia. Once you have been dismissed, the mission will end and you will acquire the mission Priority: Thessia. The mission is considered finished after talking with the Councilor. However, if you sabotaged the genophage cure *and* if Urdnot Wrex leads the krogan, he will be waiting for you at Normandy Dock: Bay D24 with a recording of your conversation with Dalatrass Linron. Enraged at this betrayal, he tries to kill Shepard. He cannot be reasoned with regardless of your choice of words. There are two Renegade interrupts that will allow you to shoot him, but in both cases Bailey and C\-Sec will take him down if you decline.
evidence.for_key: the Cerberus coup on the Citadel and Udina's betrayal

evidence.text: After the events earlier that year, the newly promoted Commander Bailey is put in charge of the C\-Sec operations for the Citadel Embassies. He personally greets Shepard upon the Commander's return to the Citadel to petition the Council's aid in retaking Earth. In personal conversations with Shepard, Bailey expresses discontentment with his promoted position. He is more akin of an administrative assistant to the Council than a C\-Sec officer. This is seen when Shepard first enters his office and witnesses Bailey attempting to calm down a news reporter demanding to see the Council. Moreover, Bailey, like many humans on the Citadel, has family left on Earth during the initial Reaper invasion. His ex\-wife's whereabouts are unknown, and he has not heard from his son and daughter once the comm buoys went down. Shepard later comes by Bailey's office to request that he release Jona Sederis, the leader of Eclipse. Aria T'Loak secretly leaned on the Council beforehand, but Bailey is desperately trying to stall, fearing what would happen if a murderous psychopath like Sederis were to be released. Shepard can either use Spectre authority to have her released or find another solution to committing Eclipse to the war effort. When Cerberus launches an unexpected assault on the Citadel, Bailey is wounded attempting to retake C\-Sec Headquarters. Luckily, Shepard arrives and dispatches Bailey's attackers. Bailey then gains access to headquarters and sets up a backup network so his fellow C\-Sec officers can plan a counterattack. He then discovers a message from the salarian councilor, who was suppose to be meet with the executor, warning that someone on the Citadel has betrayed them to Cerberus. Bailey aids Shepard in beating Kai Leng to the Council after having learned that Udina is the traitor. Bailey personally makes his way to Shepard's position, forcing Leng to flee; Bailey guesses that Leng figured that Udina's plan would fail. Following the coup, if Shepard questions Bailey if he ever suspected Udina trying to murder the Council, Bailey admits Udina always did rub him the wrong way. Bailey feels like Udina made him for an idiot and he proved Udina right, but Shepard cheers Bailey up by saying that Udina's dead and Bailey is still alive. Bailey thanks Shepard for saving him, saying if Shepard hadn't shown up, both Udina and Cerberus would have been dancing on his grave. If the genophage cure is sabotaged by Shepard with Wrex as the krogan leader, Wrex confronts Shepard in the Normandy SR\-2 docking bay and attempts to kill them. Bailey arrives with a security detail and assists Shepard in taking Wrex down. After Wrex is dead, Bailey contacts the morgue and informs them about the corpse, suggesting that the body is too heavy and needs to be spaced.
evidence.for_key: the Cerberus coup on the Citadel and Udina's betrayal

evidence.text: The Council must be informed of the Reaper threat and the Prothean device that may be able to stop the Reapers. Go to Councilor Udina's office on the Citadel and convince the Council to send help for the fight against the Reapers.

evidence.text:
This short Mass Effect 3 mission was acquired automatically after liberating Rannoch from the Reapers. The asari Councilor contacted Shepard on the vid-com claiming vital information that had to be shared in person. Returning to the Citadel, Shepard went to the late Donnel Udina's office in the Embassies, where the Councilor reported that the Asari Republics were losing badly and revealed that a Prothean artifact had been hidden for millennia in the Temple of Athame on the asari homeworld, Thessia. The conversation ended the mission and unlocked Priority: Thessia.

If Shepard had sabotaged the genophage cure and Urdnot Wrex led the krogan, Wrex was waiting at Normandy Dock: Bay D24 with a recording of Shepard's conversation with Dalatrass Linron. Enraged by the betrayal, he attacked Shepard and could not be reasoned with. Two Renegade interrupts let Shepard shoot him; otherwise Bailey and C-Sec gunned him down. Killing Wrex cost the Clan Urdnot and krogan mercenary War Assets, and the incident was afterward covered up, evidenced by an ANN mail. If Urdnot Wreav led the krogan, he never discovered the deception and remained oblivious through the end of the game. The page also documents a sequence-break exploit using the DLC rapid-transport terminals that allowed players to sabotage the cure, gain salarian support, and keep Wrex alive until the final battle in London.

evidence.text:
Citadel Arena: Cerberus Challenge was a side mission in the Mass Effect 3: Citadel DLC, available after Citadel Docks: Retake the Normandy, once the Armax Arsenal Arena opened along with the rest of Silversun Strip. After Shepard completed some arena matches, a fan named Rutaana emailed the Combat Sim Controls. Rutaana explained that some associates had heard rumors that Shepard worked with Cerberus and were intensely disappointed, and asked Shepard to fight simulated Cerberus forces publicly, alongside Alliance soldiers, to win those fans back.

To complete the challenge, Shepard selected Cerberus as the enemy at the Combat Simulator Control terminal and entered the simulation with an Alliance-only squad: no squadmates, James alone, or James plus Kaidan or Ashley if the Virmire survivor was alive and available, as no other squadmates qualified as the specified "Alliance soldier friends." Other match modifiers were unrestricted, so the challenge could be completed alongside non-conflicting arena challenges such as the Medi-Gel Challenge or Spin Zone Elite Challenge. After the match, Rutaana sent a second email saying the match was what her friends needed to see, noting that some complained a simulation meant less while others cited Shepard's role in stopping the Citadel coup. Reading the second email granted +5 Reputation.

A disturbance in the cafe area you just left alerts your squad members to the place, revealing the councilor who was under cloak the whole time. Before you can get down there, Kai Leng will arrive to ruin your party. The salarian councilor gets out the critical information that Udina is planning a coup before one of several things happens: - If Thane is alive and was met at Huerta Memorial prior to this mission, he will intervene and put up a fight against Leng, saving the salarian councilor but getting stabbed in the process. - If Thane is not around but Captain Kirrahe survived the events of Virmire, Leng will attempt to kill the councilor, but a cloaked Kirrahe will take the blow instead, dying in the process. As he was never a member of the Normandy's crew, Kirrahe's name will not appear on the ship's Memorial Wall. - If neither character is around to intervene, Leng will kill the councilor. **Note:**  If a Mass Effect 2 save has not been imported, neither Thane or Kirrahe will be present. Shepard calls Bailey, and Bailey unlocks a C\-Sec police car for Shepard's pursuit. Using transponders, Bailey determines that Udina is leading the Council to a landing pad near Shalmar Plaza, where Kai Leng is presumably waiting for them. In his spare time, though, Leng decides to interfere with Shepard by attacking the police car with his sword. This proves effective, damaging the vehicle and putting Shepard's party on foot in the Commons.

Otherwise, Kirrahe will give his life to save the Salarian councilor instead of Thane. **Military Strength:** 20 **Note:** This asset was not available in the PS3 version, until the Mass Effect Trilogy was released. Lauded by his superiors for his decisive leadership under fire, Kirrahe was promoted and decorated with the prestigious Star of Sur'Kesh. The major continues to join missions with his men, believing that nothing substitutes for experience, and that the best tactical strategies are planned on the battlefield.

evidence.text:
Acquired immediately after the events on Tuchanka and triggered by Shepard's next approach to the Citadel, this Mass Effect 3 mission responded to the salarian councilor's warning that Councilor Udina was a security risk. The Normandy was refused landing clearance; Joker contacted either Thane Krios or Armando-Owen Bailey inside the station, who reported that Cerberus had attacked and seized C-Sec Headquarters and the Docks. Shepard deployed with a squad and fought uphill through Assault Troopers, Centurions, Combat Engineers, Guardians, Turrets and newly encountered Phantoms and Nemeses, discovering that Cerberus had again used sleeper agents planted inside a target, as on Mars.

Reaching the C-Sec Executor's office, Shepard found the executor dead and the salarian councilor (Valern if the Council was saved during Sovereign's attack, otherwise Esheel) hiding under cloak. The councilor revealed that Udina was leading a coup against the Council before Kai Leng arrived. If Thane was alive and had been visited at Huerta Memorial, he intervened and was fatally stabbed shielding the councilor; if not, a cloaked Kirrahe took the blow and died; if neither was present, Leng killed the councilor. Bailey unlocked a C-Sec car, Leng disabled it with his sword, and Shepard pursued Udina and the Council on foot through the Presidium Commons, an Atlas fight, and a final zone where Cerberus reinforcements arrived by elevator cars that could be halted by shooting their power conduits.

At the landing pad the Virmire survivor (Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko), now a Spectre, blocked Shepard's path with weapon raised. A trust total built from prior choices (romance, saving the Council, keeping Kirrahe or Thane alive, hospital visits, kindness on Mars) plus a reputation check determined whether they stood down or forced a confrontation. Udina refused to step away from the door console, shoved the asari Councilor, and drew on her; Shepard or the Virmire survivor shot him dead. Kai Leng reported the failure to the Illusive Man.

Afterward, Thane could be attended in his final moments at Huerta Memorial with Kolyat present; Bailey lamented C-Sec's inability to catch Leng; Priority: Perseus Veil and numerous Citadel meetings and War Assets (asari fleets, and salarian forces if the councilor was saved) opened up. Anderson emailed the Alliance dossier on Kai Leng, and reading it before meeting Miranda let Shepard warn her of Leng, preventing her later death. The Virmire survivor could rejoin the squad or serve as a War Asset under Hackett.

evidence.text:
Kolyat Krios was the drell son of Thane and Irikah Krios. As described in Mass Effect: Foundation, Thane proclaimed him a gift from Arashu at birth but was an absent, clueless parent; Kolyat was raised by Irikah while Thane's freelance assassination jobs grew longer and farther away. When Thane's enemies attacked, Kolyat hid on his mother's instruction and was never found, but never saw Irikah alive again. He witnessed Thane's grief and breakdown while in the custody of crime scene investigators.

In Mass Effect 2, Thane had stored money with volus bankers on the Citadel as Kolyat's inheritance, but Kolyat took it early and became a hitman. Hired by Elias Kelham through information from Mouse, he was contracted to assassinate the turian politician Joram Talid in the 800 Blocks. Commander Shepard and Thane tracked Talid from separate positions to stop Kolyat from becoming a killer. If they failed to coordinate, Kolyat killed Talid and escaped; otherwise Shepard interrupted him and, with Thane, stopped the execution. Kolyat, furious at Thane's lifelong absence, calmed as his father explained why Irikah was killed and why he could not return, and called Kolyat the only good thing he ever added to the world. In the C-Sec interrogation room Kolyat could face community service, work for Captain Bailey, or go to trial; Thane stayed in contact either way.

In Mass Effect 3, if reconciled, the two remained in contact. Kolyat appeared at Thane's side after Kai Leng mortally wounded Thane during the Cerberus attack on the Citadel; despite a blood transfusion, Kepral's Syndrome made recovery impossible. At Thane's deathbed, Kolyat finished his father's prayer to Kalahira, having spent the past year with the drell priests, and led a prayer for redemption that Thane revealed was intended for Shepard. In the Citadel DLC, Kolyat emailed Shepard requesting a memorial service, held at Shepard's apartment with Thane's old crewmates and the salarian Councilor. He planned to lobby the Councilor (Valern or Esheel) to fund salarian research into Kepral's Syndrome, and told Shepard he had found three intercepted video messages from Thane addressed to the Commander.
evidence.for_key: Thane Krios dying to stop Kai Leng and protect the Salarian Councilor

evidence.text:
Thane Krios was a drell assassin, rumored the most skilled in the galaxy, who preferred to kill targets up close using stealth, firearms, hand-to-hand combat and biotics. Born in 2146, he was given by his parents at age six to the hanar to be trained as an assassin under the Compact between the two species, and made his first kill at twelve. A deeply spiritual man, he followed the old drell polytheistic religion, praying to Amonkira (lord of hunters) to find a target, Arashu (goddess of motherhood and protection) when defending another, and Kalahira (goddess of oceans and the afterlife) after a kill. His faith held body and soul as separate, letting him regard his body as a tool, though his species' eidetic memory forced him to relive every murder. He described his years of killing as a "battle sleep."

He met his wife Irikah during an assassination when she stepped into his targeting laser to save a stranger; intrigued, he sought her out and they fell in love. The hanar released him from his Compact to raise a family. He and Irikah had a son, Kolyat, but assassination work drew Thane increasingly away from home. Batarian slavers, in revenge for Thane's killings, paid the Shadow Broker for his identity and murdered Irikah. Thane hunted down everyone responsible, abandoning his clean-kill approach for torture, and afterward threw away a coin Irikah had given him, vowing to follow his path to its end.

In Mass Effect: Foundation, Thane was sent to the Citadel to judge the Cerberus agent Rasa; after spiking her drink and cornering her, he decided he "did not see murder in her soul," apologized, and carried her off with a prayer to Kalahira.

Commander Shepard first encountered him on Illium, dropping from the ceiling to assassinate Nassana Dantius. Dying of Kepral's Syndrome, Thane joined Shepard's mission against the Collectors as penance. His loyalty mission (Thane: Sins of the Father) had Shepard help stop Kolyat from becoming a hitman on the Citadel. He was a romance option for a female Shepard, calling her "siha," after "one of the warrior-angels of the goddess Arashu."

In Mass Effect 3, if he survived, Thane resided at Huerta Memorial Hospital under the name Tannor Nuara. He declined to rejoin the crew but intercepted Kai Leng during Cerberus's attack on the Citadel, dueling him to protect the salarian councilor and being stabbed through the stomach. He died in surgery, in the final stages of Kepral's Syndrome, with Shepard and Kolyat reciting a drell prayer of redemption; the prayer was Thane's wish for Shepard, not for himself. His name was added to the Normandy's memorial wall. Shepard later avenged him by killing Kai Leng.

Thane Krios: "The measure of an individual can be difficult to discern by actions alone."
Thane, on his profession, when interviewed by Cerberus: "I am merely the weapon" / "I am merely a tool of my employer."
Thane, romanced, in Shepard's quarters before the Omega 4 Relay: "Time for me is short, siha, but any I have is yours to take."
Shepard, comforting a fearful Thane before the suicide mission: "Thane... be alive with me tonight."
Thane's Prayer, recited at his deathbed: "Kalahira, mistress of inscrutable depths, I ask forgiveness. Kalahira, whose waves wear down stone and sand-- Kalahira, wash the sins from this one, and set him/her on the distant shore of the infinite spirit."
Kolyat and Shepard, continuing the prayer: "Kalahira, this one's heart is pure, but beset by wickedness and contention. Guide this one to where the traveler never tires, the lover never leaves, the hungry never starve."
Thane's spirit to a romanced Shepard after the Citadel party: "Finish it. And when you go to the sea, I will be waiting for you at the shore."
Shepard, killing Kai Leng: "That was for Thane, you son of a bitch."
evidence.for_key: Thane Krios dying to stop Kai Leng and protect the Salarian Councilor

evidence.text: Kai Leng is amongst the forces that Cerberus sends against Commander Shepard. Like Cerberus Phantoms, he is equipped with a palm device that projects a kinetic barrier, a projectile weapon in his right gauntlet, a tactical cloak and a sword for close\-range combat. Leng and a sizable contingent of Cerberus forces are deployed during Councilor Udina's attempted coup against the Citadel Council. He was close to assassinating the salarian councilor when Shepard and either Major Kirrahe or Thane Krios interferes. Leng either stabs Krios in a brief skirmish, or fires at the councilor only to hit a cloaked Kirrahe before escaping. If both Thane and the major previously died, or Thane was never spoken to before the coup attempt, Leng will successfully assassinate the councilor. In a race to get to the remaining councilors, Leng disables Shepard's skycar, but ultimately fails his mission and is forced to retreat as C\-Sec begins to regroup. As he escapes, Leng reports his failure to the Illusive Man and promises to never let Shepard get the better of him again. In the failed coup's aftermath it's revealed that Leng released a VI into the Citadel mainframe that erased all footage of himself. If the salarian Councilor was saved, Bailey presumes that Leng didn't believe Udina's plan would succeed. Leng is later sent to the Temple of Athame on Thessia, where he kills a group of scientists waiting for Shepard. Leng remains hidden as the Commander discovers a hidden Prothean Beacon, awakening a Prothean VI named Vendetta, who holds information on the final Crucible piece known as the Catalyst. Leng then reveals himself, at which point Vendetta shuts down upon detecting that he is indoctrinated. Leng requests the Commander's attention and releases a small drone that projects a hologram of the Illusive Man. The Spectre and the Illusive Man exchange words but remain unable to sway each other, so the latter orders Leng to take the VI. The Cerberus assassin then engages Shepard's team in combat but is unable gain a clear advantage, so he instructs his gunship to level the temple. The floor caves in, leaving Shepard alive but unable to act as Leng manhandles the Commander's squad, claims the data, and escapes. After the mission, Leng sends a taunting message to Shepard titled "Evacuating Thessia", disguised as asari military command: **Evacuating Thessia** --- From: Asari Military Command Good. You opened this message. This isn't actually asari military command. They're busy tending to what's left of their planet. So you survived our fight on Thessia. You're not as weak as I thought. But never forget that your best wasn't good enough to stop me. Now an entire planet is dying because you lacked the strength to win. The legend of Shepard needs to be re\-written. I hope I'm there for the last chapter. It ends with your death. \-KL Samantha Traynor is able to track Leng to Horizon, where Henry Lawson is conducting experiments on refugees on his Sanctuary compound. At the same time, the Reapers begin attacking the compound, and one of Henry's daughters is running around attempting to broadcast messages exposing Sanctuary's true operations. Leng is ordered by the Illusive Man to get Henry's research, but reminded to kill the Lawson daughter (Miranda if she's alive, or Oriana if not) only if she got in the way. Leng wounds the Lawson daughter when they meet, but otherwise leaves her alone. He manages to complete his primary objective and abandons the Lawsons to die, but is unaware that he still left enough incriminating information behind that allows Shepard's team to locate Cerberus Headquarters (or Miranda planted a tracer on him that leads directly to the HQ). During the Alliance assault on Cronos Station, Shepard can discover video logs detailing Leng's frustration with the Illusive Man's refusal to have the Commander killed. Eventually, the assassin reveals himself in the Illusive Man's office, interrupting the Commander's attempt to warn Admiral Hackett about the Catalyst being the Citadel. Leng and Shepard battle for the last time; the Commander's team versus him and groups of Assault Troopers, Phantoms, and Nemeses he periodically summons. During the fight, the Commander taunts him on his previous leg injuries and all the times he retreated in their encounters, the latter angering Leng. Despite Leng's lethal skills and numerical superiority, he's unable to overwhelm Shepard. With his shielding depleted, he soon succumbs to attacks from Shepard's squad. Despite his heavy wounds, Leng retrieves his blade and silently approaches Shepard, attempting a kill from behind. At the critical moment, Shepard detects him and counters his attack, causing him to gape in shock.

This war-asset list collected the warships and tactical expertise the salarians brought against the Reapers. Major Kirrahe (20) joined if he survived Virmire and was not killed by Kai Leng, which required talking to Thane Krios before Priority: The Citadel II so Kirrahe rather than Thane would defend the salarian councilor; Kirrahe had been decorated with the Star of Sur'Kesh for his leadership at Virmire.

The Salarian First Fleet (150) was gained by sabotaging the genophage cure during Priority: Tuchanka; it revealed that the salarians had slowed dreadnought production because STG had procured the SSV Normandy's stealth systems and the SR-2's Reaper IFF algorithms to build stealth dreadnoughts. Abandoning the Destiny Ascension instead yielded the smaller STG Task Force (70), which had quietly prepared for the Reapers' return after the Battle of the Citadel.

Dr. Mordin Solus (25), the ex-STG geneticist, was gained if he survived the Suicide Mission and was convinced to sabotage the cure; he then worked aboard the Crucible. The Salarian Special Tasks Group (35), the salarian intelligence service operating in small espionage and sabotage cells, was gained only by letting Captain Kirrahe die in Mass Effect and speaking with Lieutenant Tolan during Priority: Sur'Kesh.

evidence.text: If Kirrahe survived the events on Virmire in 2183, he is on Sur'Kesh during the Reaper invasion in 2186\. Now promoted to Major, he is present at an STG facility that runs experiments on female krogan, loitering near the elevator entrance of the base. If Kirrahe is spoken to before entering the base, he mentions that it was he who found the krogan females on Tuchanka and brought them to Sur'Kesh. He promises Shepard that regardless of what the politicians decide, he would gladly support retaking Earth. If Garrus and/or Liara is present, he greets them enthusiastically, remarking that the Reapers have a way of bringing them together. If Javik is present, Kirrahe repeatedly assumes Javik is a genetically modified drell or turian for use in some psychological tactic, rather than an actual living Prothean. When Commander Shepard descends down the facility to extract the only remaining female krogan, Cerberus launches a surprise attack, attempting to prevent Shepard from acquiring the krogan. During the fighting, Shepard encounters Kirrahe in a skirmish with Cerberus troops. Demolishing a wave of troops with a Scorpion pistol, Kirrahe expresses his pleasure at getting to work with the Commander again before covering Shepard's team in the firefight. When the Cerberus troops are defeated, Kirrahe stays behind to protect Shepard's flank while the Commander proceeds to the Species Observation Area. If Kirrahe did not survive Virmire, Lieutenant Tolan takes his place at the beginning of the mission. An unnamed soldier, in Kirrahe's stead, also attempts to cover Shepard but does not survive. Following the mission on Sur'Kesh, Major Kirrahe sends Commander Shepard an e\-mail, again promising his support against the Reapers. **Holding the line** --- From: Major Kirrahe Commander, it was a pleasure seeing you again on Sur'Kesh, even if the circumstances were less than ideal. It seems fate has decided our meetings coincide with galactic threats. So be it. To that end, I wanted to reiterate that STG will be there to help when the need arises, regardless of the political climate. You were there for us in our hour of need. We look forward to returning the favor. Best of luck, Major Kirrahe 3rd Infiltration Regiment Special Tasks Group During the Cerberus attack on the Citadel, Kai Leng threatens the salarian councilor's life. If Kirrahe is alive but Thane Krios is dead or never spoke with Shepard before the attack, then Kai Leng attempts to kill the councilor but instead shoots a cloaked Kirrahe at point blank. Kirrahe manages to limp a considerable distance in pursuit before collapsing at a door. He claims he was right in saying it was an honor fighting with the Commander again if they have shared camaraderie. Otherwise, Kirrahe quips he never liked the idea of getting old anyway. He entrusts Shepard with the assassin's pursuit before dying. Otherwise, if Thane is alive and if Shepard spoke to Thane before the attack, Thane saves the salarian councilor's life in Kirrahe's stead and is wounded in the process. If both Kirrahe and Thane are dead (or Thane hasn't been spoken to), Kai Leng succeeds in assassinating the councilor. If krogan support is lost due to Wrex's death, Kirrahe takes his place on Earth during the battle for Earth, addressing members of his unit in the same manner Wrex would have addressed his krogan.

evidence.text: - According to The Art of Mass Effect 3, early concepts of Kai Leng gave him metal legs and hard armor, but this evolved into a stealthier appearance with a coat reminiscent of the one worn by Thane Krios. evidence.text: Following their mission on Tuchanka, Shepard is contacted by the salarian Councillor, who requests a meeting on the Citadel regarding an important matter. The Councillor explains that it concerns Councillor Udina, who has been moving vast sums of money and the Councillor wishes to discuss where it is going, claiming that Shepard "won't like the news." Upon arriving at the Citadel, however, the station is worryingly silent. Scanning emergency channels, the Normandy receives a transmission from an old associate of Shepard's (either drell assassin Thane Krios, who has retired to the Citadel to enjoy his remaining life, or Commander Bailey if otherwise) who explains that the Citadel is under attack; Cerberus has hit the station in overwhelming numbers and C\-Sec are struggling to retaliate. The contact explains that Ashley/Kaidan (having recovered from the injuries sustained on Mars and been named a Spectre by Udina since then) has gone to protect the Council, while they are attempting to reach C\-Sec Headquarters, since C\-Sec cannot launch an effective counterattack while Cerberus holds it. Deploying in the shuttle, Shepard and their squad land in the middle of a pitched battle between C\-Sec and Cerberus forces outside the headquarters, helping C\-Sec Commander Bailey retake the office. Inside, Bailey uncovers intel that the salarian Councillor was meant to be meeting with the Executor, presumably to have someone important prosecuted. Given the message the Councillor sent to the Normandy, Udina is implicated. Reasoning that the Councillor is likely holed up in the Executor's office, a fairly defensible position, Shepard's squad fight their way through Cerberus' troops, but when they reach the office and extract the Councillor, they come under attack from Kai Leng, who is under orders from the Illusive Man to assassinate the Council. The salarian Councillor also reveals that Udina is collaborating with Cerberus to stage a coup. If Thane and Major Kirrahe are both dead, Leng manages to assassinate the Councillor. If one or both are alive, then one of them thwarts Leng's assassination attempt, but is mortally wounded in the process. Leng retreats to pursue the rest of the Council, with Shepard and company in hot pursuit. Despite Leng's best efforts to slow down and stop their pursuit, Shepard reaches the Council ahead of him at a shuttle pad, locking the exits to prevent Cerberus troops from getting in and a tense standoff ensues, with Ashley/Kaidan standing in their way. Shepard reveals Udina's treachery to the Council and while he attempts to deny it, the rest of the Council, after all the times they didn't listen to Shepard, begin to believe Shepard. With the Council's escape shuttle destroyed, Udina suggests overriding the lockdown and Shepard must convince the Virmire survivor to get out of the way, either managing to talk them down or being forced to shoot them. Udina, left with few options, begins to override the lock on the door. The asari councilor tries to stop him, but he pushes her to the ground and pulls a gun on her. Shepard or Kaidan/Ashley are ultimately forced to kill the human Councillor, followed by the arrival on scene of Bailey and C\-Sec reinforcements. With Udina dead and their plan thwarted, Leng and the remaining Cerberus forces retreat, while C\-Sec begins securing the station. En route back to headquarters, Leng reports his failure to the Illusive Man, who assures his agent that Udina was expendable and he has other plans in motion, though the Illusive Man does admonish Leng for letting Shepard get the better of him; Leng angrily promises it won't happen again.

evidence.text: The Illusive Man severs communication when EDI discovers and activates the Prothean VI. They find that Vendetta's security protocols have been overridden and he informs the squad that the Catalyst is in fact the Citadel; in some previous cycle, the Reaper\-made space station had been incorporated into the activation process of the Crucible to boost its power and coordinate its function through the mass relay system. After this revelation, Shepard realises it then should be relatively easy to activate the Crucible, but Vendetta has more shocking news; the Illusive Man has fled to the Citadel and warned the Reapers of the plan to destroy them. As if this wasn't enough, the Reapers have already reasserted control over the Citadel and transported it to orbit one of their conquered planets: to be precise, Earth. As Shepard attempts to contact Admiral Hackett to tell him this devastating news, he is cut off by the return of Kai Leng, who once again engages Shepard in a furious battle, aided by various Cerberus forces. This time, Shepard emerges victorious. After the fight between Shepard and Leng, Shepard goes to back to the Illusive Man's computer to activate the Prothean VI. Little does Shepard and their squad know, Leng survived the beating he took. After silently limping to the Commander, Leng raises his sword in an attempt to kill Shepard; the Commander senses the attack and in the nick of time either disarms Leng by shattering his sword or dodges Leng's attack and finishes him off with an omni\-blade stab, avenging either Thane, Kirrahe, or Miranda. If both Thane and Kirrahe are dead, the salarian councilor was assassinated, and Miranda survived the Illusive Man's orders to have her killed (or was killed during the Suicide Mission), Shepard will taunt Leng over his cowardly victory on Thessia.

evidence.text:
Ashley Madeline Williams was a human soldier who served in the Systems Alliance as a Gunnery Chief in the 2nd Frontier Division on Eden Prime. Born April 14, 2158 on the colony world Sirona, she came from a long line of Alliance soldiers. She enlisted after high school, trained in Macapá, Brazil, on Titan, and in Earth orbit, and repeatedly earned strong performance reviews but was denied advancement and shipboard postings without explanation. Her grandfather was General Williams, who surrendered the garrison at Shanxi to the turians during the First Contact War, becoming the first human to surrender to an alien force; prejudice against the "Williams curse" stalled her career.

On Eden Prime her unit, the 212, was wiped out by geth seeking a Prothean Beacon. As sole survivor, she was transferred to the SSV Normandy by Captain Anderson, replacing the slain Corporal Jenkins, and joined Commander Shepard's hunt for Saren Arterius. She was tough, blunt, religious, fond of Tennyson's poetry, and distrustful of aliens and the Citadel Council, though not xenophobic. She could become a romance option for a male Shepard, culminating in a night together before Ilos. At Virmire, Shepard could save Ashley at the cost of Kaidan Alenko's life, or vice versa.

If she survived Virmire, Ashley remained with the Alliance after Shepard's death, rose to Operations Chief, and confronted Shepard on Horizon during the Collector abductions, distrustful of Shepard's Cerberus ties. In Mass Effect 3 she returned as a Lieutenant Commander, fought on Mars where Dr. Eva critically injured her on the Illusive Man's orders, recovered at Huerta Memorial Hospital, and was offered Spectre status by Udina. During the Cerberus coup she was tasked with protecting the Councilors and, unaware Udina worked with Cerberus, confronted Shepard; depending on their rapport she could be talked down or killed. She could rejoin the Normandy or serve on Admiral Hackett's team, could resume a romance with Shepard, and could die during the final push to the conduit or survive to mourn at the Normandy memorial wall. If she died on Virmire, Kaidan Alenko took her place throughout.

evidence.text: The six choices that players can make in Mass Effect: Genesis are as follows: - Who became Shepard's love interest? - Should the Rachni Queen on Noveria be freed or destroyed? - What is the fate of Urdnot Wrex on Virmire? - Who is sacrificed on Virmire, Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko? - What happens to the Citadel Council during the Battle of the Citadel? - Who does Shepard endorse to represent humanity on the Council, David Anderson or Donnel Udina? ## - If you used Mass Effect: Genesis to customize your Mass Effect 2 playthrough with Mass Effect story decisions on the Xbox 360, and you then want to do additional Mass Effect 2 playthroughs by importing your initial Mass Effect 2 save games, you should delete Mass Effect: Genesis before attempting to start the new playthrough. If you don’t, the game will force you through the interactive comic even though you’re importing an earlier Mass Effect 2 playthrough. - If you used Mass Effect: Genesis, Miranda won't ask about your choice for human councilor on the shuttle to Minuteman Station (since your choice will be saved through the comic). - Imported playthroughs from Mass Effect still trigger Mass Effect: Genesis; the player's major choices in the game are then shown through the comic, skipping the usual dialogue wheels (the sole exception being the choice of human councilor, since the original game did not properly save that choice, though this is also autoplayed in the Mass Effect Legendary Edition due to it properly importing the choice). Choices not accounted for in the comic are still carried over. - For imported playthroughs, Genesis always depicts Benezia dying in Liara's arms, even if Liara was not brought to Noveria. - Mass Effect: Genesis does not mention some events and subjects that were part of Mass Effect, namely the mission on Feros, and the geth and their overall involvement in the game. Additionally, no assignments are explored \- they are considered unfinished. - The meeting with the Rachni Queen says she took her drones with her, but all the drones at Peak 15 were insane and Shepard had to kill them. - In Mass Effect Legendary Edition, playing through Mass Effect: Genesis is optional, with a prompt appearing before it normally plays. - Choosing not to recruit either Wrex or Garrus is not taken into account; Genesis assumes both became part of Shepard's team.

evidence.text:
Kaidan Alenko was a human Sentinel and Systems Alliance Marine, initially a Staff Lieutenant and head of the Marine detail aboard the SSV Normandy and an original member of Commander Shepard's squad, and a possible love interest for a female Shepard. Born in 2151, he gained biotic potential after in utero element zero exposure when his mother was downwind of a Singapore transport crash. He was sent to BAaT ("Brain Camp") at Gagarin Station / Jump Zero, where he formed a close bond with a girl named Rahna and was fitted with the damaging L2 implants that left him with severe migraines. When the turian instructor Commander Vyrnnus broke Rahna's arm for reaching for water, Kaidan killed him in a biotic rage; BAaT was shut down and its records sealed, and Rahna became afraid of him. He returned to the Alliance in 2173 on his own terms, refusing further biotic training, and rose to Lieutenant with several commendations before transferring to the Normandy under Captain Anderson.

Kaidan was politically conservative, cautious, and loyal to the Alliance with no sympathy for biotic extremists. He was affected by the death of his friend Richard L. Jenkins on Eden Prime. On Virmire, Shepard could save him at the cost of Ashley Williams; if he survived he became determined to make the Council heed the Reaper threat. Between games he suffered survivor's guilt after the Normandy's destruction and Shepard's apparent death, rose to Staff Commander, and in 2185 investigated Cerberus on Horizon, where he was reunited with Shepard but refused to trust a Cerberus-aligned Commander, leaving after a bitter confrontation and later sending a conciliatory email. If romanced, Shepard kept his photo in her quarters.

In Mass Effect 3, having reached Major and command of the 1st Special Operations Biotic Company, Kaidan rejoined the fight (or Ashley took his place if he died on Virmire). He was severely injured by the Cerberus gynoid on Mars, recovered at Huerta Memorial Hospital, and accepted Spectre status from Udina. During the Cerberus coup he was ordered to protect the Councilors and confronted Shepard, unaware of Udina's collusion; Shepard could talk him down or he would be killed. If he lived he could rejoin the squad or serve as a war asset, sending a farewell email. Aboard the Normandy he spoke with Shepard about Cerberus, the war's toll, his mother separated from his father, Tali, the geth, Liara after the fall of Thessia, and the hunt for Kai Leng. He could resume or begin a romance with either a male or female Shepard, with dates at Apollo's Cafe and a Canadian meal in Shepard's apartment during the Citadel shore leave. If in the squad at the final push to the conduit, he could be killed by Harbinger if the war effort was insufficient; if he survived and Shepard fell, he placed Shepard's name on the Normandy memorial wall. He was voiced by Raphael Sbarge.

evidence.text:
Donnel Udina was humanity's ambassador to the Citadel Council, succeeding Anita Goyle, and a career diplomat determined to advance human interests while avoiding actions that might endanger humanity's political standing. He was apprehensive of Commander Shepard, particularly after Shepard's induction as the first human Spectre, and repeatedly demanded irrefutable proof before acting.

In Mass Effect, Udina pushed for a human Spectre as a step toward a Council seat. He blamed Shepard for the Eden Prime mission, regretted bringing Captain Anderson into the hearing against Saren Arterius (which cleared Saren), and directed Shepard to Harkin for leads. He constantly criticized Shepard's handling of Feros, Noveria, and Virmire, and reported the Council's doubts about Shepard's Reaper warnings. When Shepard tried to warn of the Reaper invasion, Udina locked down the Normandy; Anderson countermanded the order, knocking Udina unconscious to use his computer. Udina survived Sovereign's attack on the Citadel. If the Council survived, humanity was offered a Council seat, and Shepard could nominate either Udina or Anderson.

In Mass Effect 2, if nominated, Udina became the first human Councilor with Anderson as his aide; if Anderson was Councilor, Udina served as his adviser. In Mass Effect: Retribution (2186) Udina was the human Councilor with Admiral Anderson as advisor; after Anderson's turian-assisted strikes on Cerberus, Udina threatened an investigation and Anderson resigned. In Mass Effect: Inquisition, Udina tasked Bailey with investigating Executor Pallin, promoted Bailey to Commander, and dismissed Bailey's doubts about Pallin's guilt.

In Mass Effect 3, following the destruction of Arcturus Station and the deaths of the Alliance Parliament and Prime Minister Amul Shastri, Udina became the Alliance's most powerful political figure. He supported the Crucible, instituted a colonial draft, pressed allies for resources, appointed the Virmire survivor as the second human Spectre, and converted Presidium docks into refugee housing. Desperate after the Council refused to aid Earth, Udina conspired with Cerberus in a coup to arrest the Council and seize emergency powers. The Salarian Councilor exposed him; the coup, worsened by Kai Leng's conflicting goals, became a massacre. Shepard cornered Udina, who tried to frame Shepard and open the door for Cerberus; when he shoved and threatened the Asari Councilor with a pistol, he was shot dead by Shepard or the Virmire survivor. Anderson and Shepard later speculated he might have been indoctrinated.

evidence.text:
Virmire: Assault was the climactic mission of the Virmire chain in Mass Effect, in which Commander Shepard infiltrated and destroyed Saren Arterius's research base while Captain Kirrahe's salarian teams staged a diversionary frontal assault to draw off the geth. It followed Virmire: Saren's Plan and was acquired on leaving the salarian camp. The mission ran concurrently with the assignment Virmire: Assisting Kirrahe's Team, in which Shepard could sabotage geth communications, satellite uplinks, and air support; destroying the geth flyers was required for Kirrahe to survive.

Shepard and two squadmates advanced west past a communications tower, satellite uplink tower, and refueling platform to reach the research facility, fighting geth and krogan. Entry to the base was possible through an upper warehouse door or lower maintenance underworks, where a console offered a choice to disable base alarms (more enemies for Shepard, more experience) or trigger alarms elsewhere (more enemies against Kirrahe's teams). Inside, Shepard passed cell blocks holding indoctrinated salarians, including Private Menos Avot and Lieutenant Ganto Imness, whom Shepard could release or leave to die. In Saren's genophage lab the krogan researcher Doctor Droyas and an asari assistant attacked alongside husks. The scientist Rana Thanoptis, encountered in an office, provided information on indoctrination and Sovereign and could be spared or killed; if spared she reappeared in Mass Effect 2's Dossier: The Warlord and, in Mass Effect 3, was revealed via an email to have been indoctrinated all along and to have killed herself.

Shepard activated a Prothean beacon in Saren's private lab, receiving the full vision without losing consciousness. A red hologram then revealed that Sovereign was not a Reaper ship but an actual Reaper; after a brief exchange Sovereign ended the conversation and shattered the lab's glass. Joker reported Sovereign executing an impossible maneuver. Shepard fought through krogan and geth to disable two anti-aircraft towers so the Normandy could approach. The squadmate not sent with Kirrahe brought the Normandy's drive core, converted into a nuclear bomb, and placed it by the geothermal taps. When geth dropships assaulted the bomb site, Shepard had to choose to save either Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko; the other stayed behind and died in the blast. Saren attacked from a hover-platform and, after taking damage, grabbed Shepard, then fled when the Normandy arrived. Joker outran the detonation and the base was destroyed. In the debriefing the surviving squadmate argued they were the wrong choice; the Council offered half-hearted condolences. The Virmire survivor never returned as a squadmate in Mass Effect 2 (appearing only briefly on Horizon) but became available again in Mass Effect 3.
evidence.for_key: the Virmire survivor's choice during the coup

evidence.text: The last elevator holds the Councilors as well as the Virmire survivor (Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko), who detects your landing once you jump onto the cab and immediately fires at you through the roof. The Council and Ashley/Kaidan quickly exit the elevator, only to find their escape shuttle destroyed. As Ashley/Kaidan orders their return to the elevator, Shepard and squad finally reach them, jamming the elevator door behind them to stall Cerberus' forces. Humanity's second Spectre now stands between you and the Council, gun raised. A Paragon interrupt allows you to de\-escalate the situation by lowering your own weapons, but other than that it's all about trust. A variety of factors determine whether Ashley/Kaidan can be talked down. Starting at 0, the following table details the choices that influence the Virmire survivor's overall **trust level:** | **Factor** | **Yes** | **No** | | --- | --- | --- | | Romanced Ashley/Kaidan in Mass Effect | \+2 | \+0 | | • Cheated on them in Mass Effect 2 | −1 | \+0 | | Saved the Council in Mass Effect | \+1 | −1 | | Kept Kirrahe or Thane alive through to Mass Effect 3 and save the salarian Councilor (otherwise Udina will produce a fabricated video of Shepard assassinating the salarian Councilor) | \+0 | −2 | | Shepard was kind to Ashley/Kaidan during Priority: Mars | \+1 | −1 | | Visited Ashley/Kaidan in the hospital once (when they were awake) | \+2 | \+0 | | • Admitted and/or apologized for cheating on Ashley/Kaidan (if Shepard did cheat on them in Mass Effect 2\) | \+0 | −1 | | • Visited them in the hospital a second time | \+1 | \+0 | | Lowered their weapons against Ashley/Kaidan during the final confrontation | \+1 | \+0 | **Final trust level:** | −1 or below | → Ashley/Kaidan cannot be talked down | | --- | --- | | 0–3 | → Reputation check | | 4 or higher | → Ashley/Kaidan automatically sides with Shepard | If Ashley/Kaidan sides with Shepard, they will stand down. evidence.text: *This article or section is a stub. You can help Mass Effect Wiki by expanding it.* Lexi is one of the first people to reawaken aboard Hyperion after its 600\-year voyage through dark space, helping others through their own post\-cryostasis issues. Just after finishing the medical checkup on one of Alec Ryder's children, Lexi is in the middle of telling them to hang around while their twin's being revived when the ark hits something big enough to cause momentary gravity loss. She then hurries over to the Ryder sibling's cryopod, and diagnoses that they'll have to stay in a medical coma since the revival procedure was interrupted. After the planetside mission on Habitat 7, Lexi attends to the nearly\-dead younger Ryder. The human is having a seizure due to their SAM implant overloading, so she orders them brought to SAM Node for a hardwire connection. Upon Ryder's reawakening she once again performs basic checkups, though her expression says more than her words when Ryder inquires about their father. Lexi explains that SAM is now part of the younger Ryder in ways even they don't understand. Pathfinder succession is a moot issue, since trying to untangle Ryder and SAM's connection could kill the former. She recommends bed rest for Pathfinder Ryder, though Cora Harper only allots two hours due to the impending rendezvous with the Nexus. Later, Lexi takes Dr. Carlyle's place as Pathfinder Ryder's personal physician. She always wanted a field posting and thought she'd only be waking up colonists, but the presence of hostile aliens and environments moved things a bit too fast to her liking. Since she's a specialist in alien biology, she finds that there are plenty of opportunities to dissect kett specimens in tagging along with the Tempest crew rather than back at the Hyperion. Ryder can flirt with Lexi, but the doctor explains that the human just isn't her type. She's averse to forming romantic entanglements with her patients as she needs to look at them objectively and without distractions. Lexi acts as a confidante for the Pathfinder when discussing Alec Ryder's hidden memories and offers counsel. Following Moshae Sjefa's retrieval from Voeld, Lexi attends to her and, before leaving to let Ryder talk to her, advises treating her gently as she's in a fragile state. Sometime afterward, Lexi invites Jaal Ama Darav to the medbay and presents her findings about exalted kett. After running hundreds of scans on a Chosen corpse, Lexi has determined that nothing of the original species remains, save for a few traces of genome. She disagrees with encouraging Jaal to hold out hope fixing them as the process is permanent. If Ryder agrees, Lexi explains grief is never easy. If not, Lexi thinks they'll only make Jaal's grief worse. If Ryder encouraged Jaal but began having second thoughts after hearing Lexi's point, she reasons it's because they see Jaal as a friend, not a patient, and it's her job to observe and treat. Whichever the case, Lexi reiterates she's responsible for the crew's welfare. Ryder agrees she's good at her job, and/or reminds her of her desire to study the unknown, and she got just that with a new alien species on her table. She shares her hands actually shook while making the first incision. Kett bodies were unlike anything she's ever seen before—centuries of gene\-stealing and crafted evolution—and she deems it horrible but fascinating. Beginning to feel more comfortable in her role as Tempest doctor, Lexi starts cleaning up before the body starts to smell. Due to the Pathfinder team's rather active lifestyle, Lexi can be overheard on comms recommending increased caloric intake for everyone. Peebee complains about eating more from cans, and Vetra reminds her even with trade from Aya and Kadara they still don't have enough to augment their rations. Lexi's confident the team can find a way. Lexi and Peebee are both asari, yet do not get along well aboard the Tempest. Their interactions are either arguments (that Lexi insists are "debates" as the former term is "unprofessional"), or avoidance (more on Peebee's part). Lexi is perceived as overbearing and "uptight", something that she can ask Ryder to confirm sometime before hastily changing the topic. The issue still persists in her mind, and she starts spending increasing amounts of time at the Vortex Lounge without actually drinking anything whenever the Tempest is on the Nexus. Eventually, the bartender Anan T'Mari notices Lexi's behavior and emails Ryder about it. After the escape from the Archon's flagship, Lexi voices her disapproval with SAM killing and resuscitating the Pathfinder.

evidence.text: Joker welcomes Shepard and the squad back to the Normandy with more than a bit of sarcasm, and you can voice your opinion on that. Liara then goes on to relay some of her discoveries, culminating in her theory of a recurrent galactic extinction in which the Protheans were only the latest to disappear. You have two opportunities to interject on this line of conversation, then you can tell her in three different ways the Reapers had something to do with it based on the vision from Eden Prime. However, she claims her Prothean knowledge might be useful later on, and she deems the Normandy a safe place should Saren come after her again. She grows tired from "mental exhaustion", signifying the end of the debrief. If you already finished Feros this conversation will be interesting. After a few questions Liara offers to link her mind with Shepard's to try to make sense of the vision. The joining doesn't produce any results and Liara gets tired. Dismiss the crew and you can choose to talk to the Citadel Council. If you do, you can choose to respond to their questions in whatever way. In short order, they have security concerns about Liara, and the turian Councilor questions the destruction of a Prothean site. Once you are done with the Council, various squad members will have new dialogue.
